root_causes.description: An HTTP-boundary abort fault on the payment service causes checkout's outbound gRPC call to payment to never complete normally, so checkout blocks until its 10s deadline (checkout p99=10000ms, frontend p99=10000ms). Because the abort occurs at the HTTP boundary, payment emits no completed/errored server span, leaving its own server-side error_rate (0) and latency (p99~4.9ms) metrics completely normal.

evidence.expected_baseline: payment p99 < 10ms — server side unaffected by HTTP-boundary fault
error_rate < 0.01; fault hidden at HTTP boundary so payment records no errored server span

root_causes.description: Alternative hypothesis: a network partition/boundary fault isolating payment prevents checkout's outbound call to payment from ever completing, blocking checkout until its 10s deadline; payment never receives/completes requests so its server error_rate, latency and resource metrics stay normal. Indistinguishable from http_abort by server-side metrics alone.

evidence.expected_baseline: payment request_rate steady under normal load
0 restarts — payment pod healthy and not crashed

root_causes.description: Symptom-level: checkout exhibits the latency spike (p99 pinned exactly at the 10s deadline) as the direct victim of the blocked downstream payment call. This is a propagated effect, not the originating fault.

evidence.observed_value: request_rate mean=0.010 p95=0.038 (throughput collapsed by blocked calls)

remediation_steps: Disable / roll back the flagd flag injecting the http_abort fault on the payment service to restore normal HTTP responses.
Restart the payment deployment pods to clear any stuck/aborted connection state and re-establish checkout→payment gRPC channels.
Verify checkout p99 latency returns below 500ms and frontend p99 below 200ms, confirming downstream calls complete well under the 10s deadline.
